_readme: Internal: the source of every fact on Bromic-vs-Heatstrip.pdf, page by page, for the Specification and compliance review. Not printed and not published. Built by build.js from data/retail/vs-heatstrip.json and the product frameworks.

gates.rule: The comparative test figures (warm-zone areas, temperature rise) go public only after Infrascan Rev 2 and Australian counsel have cleared them.

Low-clearance recess lines (worry-free recessing, the 180 mm cavity) go public only once each kit's Australian electrical approval is on file and the 180 mm Australian figure is confirmed (US pages say 10 in). "Safely" is not used (owner: "worry-free").

Claim register: 'warms up faster' is on hold; only 'faster in the first 5 minutes', and only after Rev 2 (Heatstrip Enhance 3200W out-heats Platinum 3400W between 5 and 10 min; the Classic 2400W data is suspect).
Claim register: never quote a percentage from the Infrascan PDFs (they divide by Bromic's figure). Publish raw m² and percentages computed here from them.

facts.fact: Platinum Smart-Heat® Electric: The heater should all but disappear: a dark glass-ceramic face, recessed flush or slim on a wall. The customer asks which heater warms more of the table: Platinum is the one measured against Heatstrip. The ceiling cavity is shallow: the low-clearance kit is fan-cooled. By the sea, the 316 Marine model. Controls: Affinity Smart-Heat® Dimmer or On/Off, and a manual wall switch.

facts.fact: Tungsten Smart-Heat® Electric Series II: The heater is part of the look: black, white or graphite, front included, with three front patterns. The ceiling is pitched, or the heat needs a single post or a tilt toward the seats. The customer wants the longest cover: 3 years on the heater and 7 on the elements. By the sea, Coastal. Controls: Affinity Smart-Heat® Dimmer as standard, On/Off where dimming is not wanted, and a manual wall switch.
